'''Watarai Okunitamahime Shrine''' (度会大国玉比賣神社, *Watarai Ōkunitamahi-me Jinja*) is an auxiliary shrine (摂社) of {{ill|Toyōke Daijingū|ja|豊受大神宮|2=ja|3=豊受大神宮|4=zh|5=豐受大神宮|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Toyōke Daijingū|13=User:Immanuelle/Toyōke Daijingū|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} (the Outer Shrine) of {{ill|Ise Grand Shrine|en|Ise Shrine|qid=Q687168|lt=Ise Grand Shrine}}. It is located in the forested area of the Outer Shrine precincts, to the southwest of the former {{ill|Toyomiyazaki Bunko|en|Toyomiyazaki Bunko|qid=Q21653850|lt=Toyomiyasaki Bunko}}.

== Overview ==

{{ill|Watarai Okunitama-hime Shrine|lt=Watarai Okunitama-hime Shrine|lt=Watarai Ōkunidama-hime Shrine|ja|度会大国玉比賣神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Watarai Ōkunidama-hime Shrine|qq=}} is located within the sacred forest ({{ill|Jingū-rin|ja|神宮林|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Jingū-rin|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}) of {{ill|Toyōke Daijingū|ja|豊受大神宮|2=ja|3=豊受大神宮|4=zh|5=豐受大神宮|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Toyōke Daijingū|13=User:Immanuelle/Toyōke Daijingū|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} in {{ill|Toyokawachō|ja|豊川町 (伊勢市)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Toyokawa-chō, Ise|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q17223204}}, {{ill|Ise, Mie|en|Ise, Mie|qid=Q328067|lt=Ise, Mie}}, {{ill|Mie Prefecture|en|Mie Prefecture|qid=Q128196|lt=Mie Prefecture}}. It is not directly connected to the main approach (参道) of the precinct, but its entrance can be found along the boundary of the Gekū's sacred grounds. Among the auxiliary shrines of the Gekū, it Ranks fourth, following {{ill|Kusanagi Shrine (Ise)|ja|草奈伎神社、大間国生神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kusanagi Shrine (Ise)|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} and {{ill|Watarai Kunimi Shrine|ja|度会国御神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Watarai Kunimi Shrine|qq=}}<ref name="is">Sakurai (1998): p. 85</ref>.

The enshrined deities are {{ill|Kunitama|ja|大国玉命|lt=Ōkunidama no Mikoto|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kunitama|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} and {{ill|Mizusasarahime no Mikoto|ja|弥豆佐佐良比賣命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mizusasarahime no Mikoto|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}<ref name="ib">Ise Bunkasha (2008): p. 37</ref>, both considered the {{ill|Gentry|en|Gentry|qid=Q844586|lt=Chinjugami}} (local tutelary deities) of the Watarai region<ref name="ib"/>. It is said that when {{ill|Amihiwake no Mikoto|ja|天日別命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ame-no-Hiwake no Mikoto|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q106107046}}, the ancestor of the {{ill|Ise no Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja|伊勢国造|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kuni no Miyatsuko of Ise|13=User:Immanuelle/Ise no Kuni no Miyatsuko|qq=}}, visited to pacify Ise during the reign of {{ill|Emperor Jimmu|en|Emperor Jimmu|qid=Q200188|lt=Emperor Jimmu}}, these two deities welcomed him by creating a bridge with their bows<ref name="ib"/>. Notably, Ame-no-Hiwake no Mikoto’s son, {{ill|Hikokunimigaki Takeyotsuka no Mikoto|ja|彦国見賀岐建与束命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hikokunimigaki Takeyotsuka no Mikoto|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, is enshrined at Watarai Kunimi Shrine.

The precinct is surrounded by dense, towering trees, creating an atmosphere of deep shade even during the day<ref name="ib"/>. The shrine building is enclosed by a sacred fence ({{ill|Sacred fences|en|Tamagaki|qid=Q3078312|lt=Tamagaki}}), as seen in photos. There is no offering box. Beyond Watarai Ōkunidama-hime Shrine, further into the forest, lie the auxiliary shrines {{ill|Igari Shrine|ja|伊我理神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Igari Shrine|qq=}} and {{ill|Igari Shrine|ja|井中神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Inaka Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 伊我理神社|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11379372}}.

== History ==

Originally referred to as the Shrine of Watarai no Ōkunidama-hime (度会之大国玉姫の社), the shrine’s name was later standardized to Watarai Ōkunidama-hime Shrine, following its listing in the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Jinmyōchō|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Jinmyōchō|qq=}}<ref name="is"/>.

Regarding this shrine, {{ill|Katsunoshin Sakurai|ja|櫻井勝之進|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sakurai Katsunosuke|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11544758}} wrote:

{{Quotation|When a society is unified under a central authority and integrated into the nation’s structure, the deities worshipped there are also incorporated as supreme national gods or organized as deities with divine lineage or connections. This is evident in myths describing the relationship between ancient {{ill|Izumo|ja|出雲|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izumo|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11395836}} and the central government.
|Sakurai Katsunosuke, *Ise Jingū*, p. 35}}

This suggests that when the influential {{ill|Watarai clan|ja|度会氏|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Watarai clan|qq=}} of {{ill|Q11588058|ja|磯部 (部民)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Isobe|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 磯部|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11588058}} was entrusted with the worship of {{ill|Toyouke-hime|ja|豊受大御神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Toyouke-Ōmikami|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to トヨウケビメ|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q2983724}}, the clan’s ancestral deities were also incorporated into the Ise Grand Shrine’s pantheon<ref name="ij">Sakurai (1998): p. 35</ref>. Sakurai inferred that the shrine’s name indicates its role as a clan deity<ref name="ij"/>.

Although the exact date of establishment is unknown<ref name="egs">Furan Ken, "[https://web.archive.org/web/20131220190342/http://www.geocities.jp/engisiki/ise/bun/is080137-01.html Watarai Ōkunidama-hime Shrine]" (Accessed September 22, 2012)</ref>, it is believed to have existed before its incorporation into the Gekū, that is, prior to the 22nd year of {{ill|Emperor Yūryaku|en|Emperor Yūryaku|qid=Q357235|lt=Emperor Yūryaku}}’s reign. Unlike many other auxiliary shrines that experienced interruptions in ritual practices during the medieval period, Watarai Ōkunidama-hime Shrine has continuously maintained its rituals and original location up to the present day<ref name="egs"/>.

Fragments of {{ill|Sue pottery|en|Sue pottery|qid=Q7634351|lt=Sue pottery}} pottery have been discovered at the site<ref>Ise City (2011): p. 364</ref>, with most identified as Sue pottery<ref>Ise City (2011): p. 370</ref>.

== Access ==

;To Gekū Front
* About a 15-minute walk from JR {{ill|Sangū Line|en|Sangū Line|qid=Q872023|lt=Sangū Line}} or {{ill|Yamada Line (Kintetsu)|en|Yamada Line (Kintetsu)|qid=Q900630|lt=Kintetsu Yamada Line}} Ise City Station (south exit).
* 15-minute walk from the Mie Kōtsū "Ise City Station" bus stop.
* Approximately 10-minute walk from the Mie Kōtsū "Gekū-mae" bus stop.
* About 5 minutes by car from {{ill|Ise-nishi itnerchange|ja|伊勢西インターチェンジ|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ise-Nishi Interchange|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q10884865}} on the {{ill|Ise Expressway|en|Ise Expressway|qid=Q6079578|lt=Ise Expressway}}, heading north on Mie Prefectural Route 32 (Mokimoto Road). Parking is available nearby, though it requires an additional 13-minute walk from the parking lot<ref>Jingū Administration Office, "[http://www.isejingu.or.jp/mobile/i/parking/index.html Parking Information]" (Accessed September 22, 2012)</ref>.

;From Gekū Front to the Shrine
* Follow Mokimoto Road in the direction of {{ill|Shima, Mie|en|Shima, Mie|qid=Q338009|lt=Shima, Mie}} along the boundary of the sacred forest. The shrine entrance is located southwest of the former {{ill|Toyomiyazaki Bunko|en|Toyomiyazaki Bunko|qid=Q21653850|lt=Toyomiya-zaki Bunko}} site. Ascend the moss-covered stone steps to reach the shrine building<ref name="ib"/>.
